title: Peso weakens for a second straight day
teaser: Credit card installment and cash advance fees go up, Cebu Pacific loss nears P13 billion, Tax exemption plan: nothing to file yet

sections.headline: Peso weakens for a second straight day
sections.body: The peso lost ground against the US dollar for a second straight trading day on Thursday, and the main stock index slipped too. *Manila Times*: [Peso, PSEi post losses](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/peso-psei-post-losses/2468843). RCBC chief economist Michael Ricafort linked the drop to a stronger US dollar after US inflation came in hotter than expected: prices rose 0.4%, above the 0.3% forecast. That raised the odds of a future US Federal Reserve rate hike, meaning the US central bank could make dollar borrowing more expensive, which tends to pull money toward the dollar. The PSEi, the index of the biggest listed companies, fell 0.57 percent to 5,660.55 as investors weighed BMI's cut to its Philippine growth forecast. For the family, a weaker peso stretches each dollar of padala, but it can also lift the presyo of imported goods and fuel. Ricafort expects the usual Christmas rise in OFW remittances to lend the peso some support. Whether the Fed actually raises rates is still unknown.

items.text: *GMA Money*: [Peso slides to P63.7:$1](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/1009277/peso-slides-to-p63-7-1/story/) reports Ricafort's view that seasonal OFW remittances, export sales and other dollar conversions ahead of Christmas should support the peso in the fourth quarter.

sections.socialHook: The peso weakened again on Thursday after hotter US inflation data. Here is what it means for the padala and for prices at home.
sections.soWhat: Your dollar padala stretches further in pesos, but imported goods and fuel at home may cost more; compare remittance fees, not just rates.

sections.headline: Credit card installment, cash advance fees rise
sections.body: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) kept the 3 percent monthly cap on finance charges for regular credit card purchases, equal to 36 percent a year, but raised two other ceilings. *Manila Times*: [Monthly ceiling for credit card finance charges stays](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/monthly-ceiling-for-credit-card-finance-charges-stays/2468858). The maximum monthly add-on rate for installment loans goes to 1.5 percent from 1 percent. An add-on rate is interest charged each month on the original amount borrowed. The maximum one-time processing fee on a cash advance rises to P300 from P200 per transaction. The BSP said the changes aim to balance consumer protection with access to credit as issuers' costs rise. The new ceilings, under BSP Circular 1242, apply only to new transactions from the effectivity date, 15 calendar days after publication. Existing installment plans keep their agreed terms. Still unknown: the exact effectivity date, and how much each bank will actually raise its own fees, since these are ceilings, not required rates.

items.text: *Inquirer Business*: [BSP keeps 3% cap on credit card finance charges](https://business.inquirer.net/620498/bsp-keeps-3-cap-on-credit-card-finance-charges) also reports the retained cap.

sections.socialHook: Credit card cash advances can soon cost up to P300 per transaction in processing fees, up from P200. Installment rates go up too.
sections.soWhat: Before a new installment plan or cash advance for Christmas, ask your bank for its updated rate and fee; existing plans stay the same.

sections.headline: Cebu Pacific loss nears P13 billion
sections.body: Cebu Pacific reported a net loss of almost P13 billion for January to September, a reversal from a profit of about P9.5 billion a year earlier. Reports differ slightly on the exact figure: P12.84 billion per *PhilStar*: [Cebu Pacific widens loss to nearly P13 billion](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/13/2569696/cebu-pacific-widens-loss-nearly-p13-billion), and P12.78 billion per the Manila Times. Revenue grew about 10 percent as the airline flew 20.77 million passengers, but expenses rose 24 percent to P99.23 billion. Higher jet fuel prices, tied to tensions in the Middle East, and a weaker peso drove the costs. The carrier also said it paid more for aircraft servicing because of new fees applied by airport operators. Why it matters: Cebu Pacific is the country's largest carrier and the way many kababayan fly home. The coverage does not mention any fare changes, so it is unknown whether these costs will reach ticket prices. The airline said holiday bookings remain healthy.

items.text: *Manila Times*: [Cebu Pacific reports P12.78B Jan-Sept. loss](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/corporate-news/cebu-pacific-reports-p1278b-jan-sept-loss/2468806) reports fuel expenses jumped 62.4 percent to P39.1 billion and foreign exchange losses quadrupled to P5.03 billion. CEO Michael Szucs said: "The third quarter remained a challenging period, as elevated fuel prices, a weaker peso, and broader macroeconomic pressures continued to affect our operations."

*Inquirer Business*: [High fuel prices, peso slump ground CebuPac to P12.8-B loss](https://business.inquirer.net/620570/high-fuel-prices-peso-slump-ground-cebupac-to-p12-8-b-loss) also covers the results.

sections.socialHook: Cebu Pacific lost almost P13 billion in nine months as jet fuel and a weaker peso pushed up costs. Holiday bookings are still healthy, it says.
sections.soWhat: Flying home for the holidays? Compare the full fare including taxes and airport fees before paying; no fare change is reported yet.

sections.headline: Tax exemption plan: nothing to file yet
sections.body: This is a heads-up, not an action item. A bill, House Bill 10345, would raise the yearly income tax-free threshold from P250,000 to P350,000 of taxable income. *Manila Times*: [Who benefits from the proposed P350K income tax exemption?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/who-benefits-from-the-proposed-p350k-income-tax-exemption/2468816). At P350,000, a worker would save about P15,000 a year, or P1,250 a month. Those at or below P250,000 see no change. The bill was referred to the House Ways and Means committee on July 29 and is not law. Nothing changes in payslips yet.
sections.socialHook: A proposed bill could save some workers about P1,250 a month in income tax. It is not law yet, so payslips stay the same for now.
sections.soWhat: Family members working locally should not expect a bigger take-home pay yet; the tax exemption bill is still in committee.

sections.headline: Sabi nila

items.leadIn: PhilStar Opinion column (columnist not named in our material)
items.text: The column "Higher electric bills due to El Niño" relays Meralco spokesman Joe Zaldarriaga downplaying fears of power shortages and rate hikes from a Super El Niño projected to last until mid-next year: "So from the standpoint of power supply adequacy, we are prepared to serve our customers." [Read the column](https://www.philstar.com/opinion/2026/11/13/2569764/higher-electric-bills-due-el-nio)

sections.socialHook: Will El Niño push up the Meralco bill? A PhilStar column relays what Meralco's spokesman says about supply and rates.

sections.headline: Iba pang balita

items.text: Wholesale prices of construction materials in Metro Manila rose 3.7% year on year in October, the fastest since August 2023, led by structural steel, the PSA said. Retail prices rose 2%. *BusinessWorld*: [Metro Manila wholesale construction materials price growth in October hits three-year high](https://bworldonline.com/economy/2026/11/12/793593/metro-manila-wholesale-construction-materials-price-growth-in-october-hits-three-year-high/)

The NFA raised its palay buying price to P30 per kilo and says farmers may earn up to P8 per kilo after costs. It can now buy up to 500 bags per cropping season from each farmer, up from 200. *GMA Money*: [Farmers may earn up to P8 per kilo as palay buying price rises --NFA](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/1009233/farmers-may-earn-up-to-p8-per-kilo-as-palay-buying-price-rises-nfa/story/)

Following up on this week's growth and rate stories, the BSP said it will factor in weak demand when setting interest rates, while still working to bring inflation back to its 3% target by 2028. It has raised its key rate by 125 basis points in 2026. *PhilStar*: [BSP weighs weak growth as inflation stays elevated](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/13/2569703/bsp-weighs-weak-growth-inflation-stays-elevated) and [Philippines faces difficult mix of high inflation, sluggish growth — BSP](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/12/2569657/philippines-faces-difficult-mix-high-inflation-sluggish-growth-bsp)

sections.socialHook: Also today: steel pushes building material prices to a three-year high, palay gets a better NFA price, and the BSP weighs a slowing economy.

sections.headline: Noong araw

items.text: On this day, House Speaker Manny Villar passed the articles of impeachment against President Joseph Estrada. Impeachment, where the House formally charges an official and the Senate sits as the court, is again in the news this year. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines)

sections.socialHook: On this day in 2000, the House passed the articles of impeachment against President Joseph Estrada.
